tool_input.content:
feat(validate-content): check the deposited guide against the embed

The doc fix in 32a9753 requires internal/enable/guide/CLAUDE.md and
.punt-labs/ethos/CLAUDE.md to be byte-identical. Nothing enforced that.
checkSetupSync has covered ETHOS-SETUP.md since DES-071; the guide
sitting beside it was held only by whoever remembered to edit both
copies. Shipping a hand-enforced invariant inside a fix for a false
claim is the same defect one level up, so checkGuideSync now compares
the deposited copy to enable.Guide — the bytes that actually ship, for
the reason checkReadmeTable already states: an on-disk comparison can be
fooled by a copy that differs from the build.

Drift here is not cosmetic. This repo dogfoods `ethos enable`, so the
deposited guide IS enable's output; when it diverges, every agent
working in this repo reads guidance no consumer receives. That is how
the false self-install rule survived four months past the commit that
disproved it.

Falsified rather than assumed. Appending one byte to the real deposited
guide produces:

  FAIL  enable: CLAUDE.md guide embed sync: .punt-labs/ethos/CLAUDE.md
  and internal/enable/guide/CLAUDE.md have drifted — run `ethos enable`
  to redeposit the guide

Running that remedy restored sync and touched nothing else. The unit
test covers in-sync, one byte of drift, and never-deposited; minimalRepo
now deposits the guide the way it already deposited the setup doc.

The false text appears in five live files, not three. The two not
touched here are tests/e2e/fixtures/ethos-self/{docs/development.md,
.punt-labs/ethos/CLAUDE.md}. That fixture is a point-in-time whole-repo
snapshot (inherited via 9e08141), already drifted in three unrelated
passages, and its only assertion is a 470000-byte ceiling insensitive to
a ~100-byte edit. Partially refreshing it yields a snapshot matching no
real moment, which is worse than one that is honestly old. A wholesale
refresh is its own change.
